original.:question/problem: Use a calculator to evaluate ${log}_{18}(41)$ rounded to $3$ decimal places.
original.:question/worked-solution:
Let's calculate ${log}_{18}(41)$ by changing the base $18$ to the common logarithm (base $10$).

We use the change of base formula:

$$
{log}_{a}X=\frac{{log}_{b}X}{{log}_{b}a}
$$

In our case, $a=18,$ $X=41,$ $b=10.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{18}(41) & =\frac{{log}_{10}(41)}{{log}_{10}(18)} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{log}(41)}{\operatorname{log}(18)} \\  & \approx \frac{1.612\,784}{1.255\,273} \\  & \approx 1.285\end{aligned}
$$

original.:question/problem: Use a calculator to evaluate $\log_3 (7)$ rounded to $2$ decimal places.
original.:question/worked-solution:
Let's calculate $\log_3 (7)$ by changing the base $3$ to the common logarithm (base $10$).

We use the change of base formula:

$$
\log_a X = \dfrac {\log_b X} {\log_b a}
$$

In our case, we have $a=3,$ $X =7,$ and $b=10.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{3}⁡(7) & =\frac{{log}_{10}⁡(7)}{{log}_{10}⁡(3)} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(7)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(3)} \\  & ≈\frac{0.845\,10}{0.477\,12} \\  & ≈1.77.\end{aligned}
$$
